==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=SqlServer&min=SqlServer&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Verify.SqlServer: subscribes to the Microsoft.Data.SqlClient diagnostic listener, so every
        // command executed while a recording is running is added to the snapshot under the name sql.
        // Registers the schema converter for SqlConnection either way.
        VerifySqlServer.Initialize();

        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Extensions/SqlServerTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=SqlServer&min=SqlServer&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using Microsoft.Data.SqlClient;
using VerifyTests.SqlServer;

// Verify.SqlServer: Snapshots a SQL Server database schema, and records every command executed on a connection.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.SqlServer
// Note: Recorded SQL is reformatted before it is written, so a snapshot is stable against
// whitespace and bracket differences in the command text.
// Note: Recording.Stop() returns the entries instead of adding them; a failed command arrives as
// an ErrorEntry.
// Note: DbObjects and the objects a SchemaFilter sees are in the VerifyTests.SqlServer namespace
// (plan A7).
// Note: Initialize can only run once per process, so a project needing both the recording and the
// non-recording variant needs two test assemblies.
// Note: Scripting the schema uses SQL Server Management Objects, which is a large dependency.
// Note: The obsolete SchemaSettings(...) is replaced by SchemaIncludes and SchemaFilter.
public class SqlServerTests
{
    // Verifying the connection scripts the whole schema into a snapshot, so a migration that
    // changes a table, a view or a stored procedure shows up as a reviewable diff.
    // Not run by default: needs a SQL Server instance reachable at the connection string in this file.
    [Fact(Skip = "needs a SQL Server instance reachable at the connection string in this file.")]
    public async Task Schema()
    {
        await using var connection = new SqlConnection(connectionString);
        await connection.OpenAsync();

        await Verify(connection);
    }

    // Everything executed between Recording.Start() and the verification is added under the
    // name sql, so the snapshot shows both the result and the SQL that produced it.
    // The recorded text is reformatted first, so it reads the same however it was built.
    // Not run by default: needs a SQL Server instance reachable at the connection string in this file.
    [Fact(Skip = "needs a SQL Server instance reachable at the connection string in this file.")]
    public async Task RecordCommands()
    {
        await using var connection = new SqlConnection(connectionString);
        await connection.OpenAsync();
        Recording.Start();

        await using var command = connection.CreateCommand();
        command.CommandText = "select Value from MyTable";
        var value = await command.ExecuteScalarAsync();

        await Verify(value!);
    }

    // Points at a local SQL Server. Selecting LocalDb as well builds a database per test.
    const string connectionString = "Server=(local);Database=Sample;Integrated Security=true;Encrypt=false";
}

==== interactions

Warning external-tool: SqlServer needs A SQL Server instance: the samples open a connection to a local SQL Server. Selecting LocalDb as well gives each test a database of its own instead.
